name: DHEA

lead: DHEA is a hormone made by the adrenal glands that the body turns into testosterone and estrogen. Levels fall with age, which is why it is sold as an anti-aging and hormone-support supplement.
Trials support the vaginal form for menopausal atrophy. For muscle, skin or looks in healthy people, evidence is limited.

paras: It acts mostly as a precursor converted in tissues to androgens and estrogens, plus some direct activity in the brain. Its sulfate form, DHEA-S, acts as a long-lasting reservoir.

In the US it is sold over the counter, but some countries restrict it and it is prohibited in sport. Because it converts to sex hormones, hormonal effects are possible; users on testosterone therapy report mixed experiences.

lead: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA, also called androstenolone or prasterone) is an endogenous steroid precursor and one of the most abundant circulating steroids in humans. It is made mainly by the adrenal glands, with smaller amounts from the gonads and brain, and serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of androgens and estrogens; it also has weak direct hormonal and neurosteroid effects [1][2][3]. Its sulfate ester, DHEA-S, is a stable marker of adrenal androgen activity [4].

Blood levels peak around age 20 and fall steadily with age, a pattern called adrenopause. This decline underlies its promotion as an anti-aging and testosterone-supporting supplement [1][5]. In the United States DHEA is sold over the counter as a supplement and as the prescription product prasterone [1]. Published trials support medical use in some situations such as vaginal atrophy, while evidence for appearance and body composition benefits in healthy people is limited [6][7].
infobox: Oral; vaginal insert (prasterone); injectable forms exist [1]
US dietary supplement; prasterone is a prescription product [1]

paras: DHEA is produced in the zona reticularis of the adrenal cortex and rises at adrenarche, when it is considered responsible for early pubic and axillary hair, body odor and oily skin through conversion to more potent androgens [4]. It is converted to androstenedione and then testosterone, and to estrogens, in peripheral tissues; a looksmax.org guide states that about 5 percent or less of circulating testosterone in men derives from DHEA [8]. Reviews also describe actions in the brain and on cell membrane receptors [3][2].

Vaginal DHEA (prasterone) has been studied in phase 3 trials for vaginal atrophy in postmenopausal women [9][10][11]. Evidence reviews cover its use in genitourinary syndrome of menopause [12], and a network meta-analysis examined DHEA for poor ovarian response in IVF [13]. One review states that clinical evidence supports use in hypoadrenal states [3]. Blood DHEA and DHEA-S are used to evaluate excess adrenal androgen production [1].

People take oral DHEA hoping for higher testosterone, better skin, energy, libido, muscle and a more youthful look. The skin and anti-aging claims are described by looksmax.org posters [8]. Review articles describe broad pharmacological effects on organ systems while noting that these remain areas of research [3][5].

Early randomized work in older adults gave replacement-dose DHEA for several months and examined hormones, IGF-I and perceived well-being [14]. A 1999 randomized trial of DHEA replacement in aging humans is also in the literature [15]. A review of adrenopause by a Japanese group described DHEA as having beneficial anti-aging effects on the immune system, metabolism and brain, while noting that DHEA has few intrinsic androgenic actions [5].

Registered phase 3 trials enrolling several hundred postmenopausal women evaluated intravaginal DHEA for atrophy symptoms [9][10][11], and a phase 2 trial studied it in pulmonary hypertension in COPD [16]. A review of fertility adjuncts reported on DHEA in IVF with poor responders [13]. No trial in the sources reviewed shows that oral DHEA in healthy people improves muscle mass, height or facial appearance.

Oral bioavailability is about 50 percent, with liver metabolism. DHEA has a half-life of about 15 to 30 minutes, whereas DHEA-S lasts 7 to 11 hours and circulates at roughly 250 to 300 times the DHEA concentration, forming a reservoir that can be converted back to DHEA in tissues [1]. DHEA crosses the blood-brain barrier readily [1]. A specific nuclear DHEA receptor has not been identified, though membrane receptors have been reported [3]; in 2011 researchers reported that DHEA and DHEA-S bind neurotrophin receptors [1].

DHEA is available without prescription as a supplement in the US [1]. Some posters on looksmax.org say it is banned or restricted as a steroid in their own countries [8]. US product labels for homeopathic hormone products listing DHEA carry the statement that their claims have not been reviewed by the FDA [17].

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and TRT communities
paras: On looksmax.org, DHEA is promoted in a guide as a "youth hormone" that supports skin collagen and should be kept at the high end of normal [8]. A thread cites claims that the nutrition writer Ray Peat gained height in his forties by taking it, which other users doubted [18]. On T Nation, users on testosterone therapy discuss whether to add DHEA, with mixed reports: one said 25 mg a day raised free testosterone while their doctor saw no need, another said they felt worse when taking it [19][20][21]. Another post argued that low DHEA-S indicates adrenal weakness but that supplementing does not repair it [22].

lore.intro: DHEA is discussed on looksmax.org as an anti-aging, skin and hormone-support supplement, and on T Nation mainly by men on testosterone therapy asking whether it adds anything [8][19][21].
